subject: human-resources
intro: Human resources is the people profession inside every employer, and its graduates are paid to hire, develop, reward and defend workforces — with analytics and strategy increasingly on top.

roles.title: Human Resources Specialists
roles.what: Recruit, screen, interview and place individuals within an organisation, and often handle further activities across multiple human resources areas such as onboarding, records and employee support.
roles.where: The talent acquisition unit — workforce planning, recruitment and selection, onboarding — mirrors the role directly, and the employment law basics from the HR foundations unit set the compliance boundaries specialists work within.

roles.title: Human Resources Managers
roles.entry: Bachelor's degree plus years of experience
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate human resources activities and staff, owning hiring, compensation, labour and development policy at organisational level, usually after years in specialist roles.
roles.where: The employee relations unit's engagement, discipline and collective relations work, plus total rewards and pay equity from the compensation unit, are the manager-level decisions, with HR analytics and strategy as the modern dashboard.

roles.title: Training and Development Specialists
roles.what: Design or conduct work-related training and development programs that improve individual skills or organisational performance, analysing training needs and evaluating whether the training worked.
roles.where: The learning and development unit — training design and transfer, career development, performance management — is the profession's textbook, with the HR analytics unit's measurement mindset behind the evaluation half of the job.

roles.title: Labor Relations Specialists
roles.what: Resolve disputes between workers and managers, negotiate collective bargaining agreements, and coordinate grievance procedures that handle employee complaints.
roles.where: The employee relations and engagement unit — grievance and discipline, unions and collective relations — plus employment law basics from unit one give the legal and procedural grounding this bargaining-table role demands.

roles.title: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
roles.what: Run an employer's compensation and benefits programs and job analysis, specialising in areas such as position classification and pension programs, and keeping pay systems fair and lawful.
roles.where: The total rewards unit — compensation structures, benefits, pay equity and transparency — maps one-to-one onto the role, and people analytics from the HR analytics unit supplies the benchmarking data the pay decisions rest on.
